chunks: From him, from his father, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Hamza Al-Thumali, from Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said:

When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, gathers the former and the latter, a caller will stand and call out, making the people hear, and he will say: 'Where are those who love for the sake of Allah?' He said: 'So a neck (group) of the people will rise, and it will be said to them: Go to Paradise without reckoning.'

He said: 'So the angels will meet them and say: To where?' They will say: 'To Paradise without reckoning.' He said: 'So they will say: So which group of people are you?' They will say: 'We are those who love for the sake of Allah.' He said: 'So they will say: And what were your deeds?' They will say: 'We used to love for Allah and hate for Allah.' He said: 'So they will say: Excellent is the recompense of the workers.'

key_terms.الْمُتَحَابُّونَ فِي اللَّهِ: Those who love each other purely for the sake of Allah
key_terms.عُنُقٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ: A neck/group of people (idiom for a distinct group)
key_terms.نُعْطِشُ فِي اللَّهِ: To hate for the sake of Allah (contextual)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for those who love each other for the sake of Allah in the afterlife?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Al-Kafi highlights 'al-wala' wa al-barra' (loyalty and enmity for God) as a supreme criterion for salvation, emphasizing that sincere mutual love transcends the need for detailed accounting (hisab). The scene illustrates the divine recognition of this spiritual bond, where angels confirm their status not by ritual deeds alone, but by their alignment with God's will through love and hatred. This underscores the Shia emphasis on the heart's orientation towards the Divine as the essence of faith.
